BATON ROUGE, LA. — Southern University men's basketball will face a demanding test from the opening tip of the 2026-27 season as the Jaguars announced their upcoming schedule, featuring a challenging non-conference slate featuring matchups against programs from the ACC, Big East, Big Ten, Missouri Valley, Mountain West, SEC and West Coast. Along with three regular-season home contests at the F. G. Clark Activity Center.

The Jaguars will open the season with one of the more challenging stretches on the schedule, playing five consecutive road games against NCAA Division I opponents. Southern begins the campaign Monday, Nov. 2 at Southern Methodist University before traveling to Texas Christian University on Friday, Nov. 6.

The road swing continues Sunday, Nov. 8 at Drake University, followed by a Tuesday, Nov. 10 match up at Iowa State University and a Thursday, Nov. 12 contest at the University of Minnesota.

"We're excited about the challenges our schedule presents this season," said Southern head coach Kevin Johnson. "Our non-conference schedule will give us an opportunity to compete against some very good basketball programs, and we believe those experiences will help prepare us for the intensity and rigors of SWAC play. We want to challenge our team early, learn from each game and continue to grow as we get ready for conference competition. We're looking forward to the opportunity and can't wait to get the season started."

Southern will return home for its first home contest of the season on Tuesday, Nov. 17, hosting Louisiana Christian University at 11:00 a.m for field trip day game 1. The Jaguars will close out November with another pair of road challenges, traveling to the University of Nebraska on Nov. 25 before facing Vanderbilt University on Nov. 27.

The Jaguars will continue non-conference play in December, hosting Champion Christian College on Tuesday, Dec. 1 at 11:00 a.m. for field trip day game 2, before embarking on another challenging stretch on the road. Southern will travel to Fresno State University on Dec. 5 and later make a trip west for contests at the University of Oregon on Dec. 16, the University of the Pacific on Dec. 18 and the University of California on Dec. 20.

SU closes out its non-conference schedule at home Monday, Dec. 28 against Southern University-New Orleans at 2:00 p.m.

The Jaguars open Southwestern Athletic Conference play on the road Saturday, Jan. 2 at Texas Southern before traveling to Prairie View on Monday, Jan. 4.

Southern will make its home conference debut Saturday, Jan. 9 against Florida A&M. The Jags will remain at home to host Bethune-Cookman on Monday, Jan. 11, followed by Grambling State on Saturday, Jan. 16.

After a pair of road contests at Arkansas-Pine Bluff and Mississippi Valley State, SU returns home to host Alcorn State on Saturday, Jan. 30. The Jaguars will then welcome Jackson State to Baton Rouge on Monday, Feb. 1.

The second half of the conference schedule features road contests at Alabama A&M and Alabama State before Southern returns home for consecutive contests against Prairie View on Feb. 13 and Texas Southern on Feb. 15.

SU will close out the regular season with four road games and two home contests, including a pair of home games against Alabama State on Tuesday, March 2 and Alabama A&M on Thursday, March 4. 

The 2027 Southwestern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Tournament is scheduled for March 8-13 at the Gateway Center in Atlanta, Georgia.

BATON ROUGE, LA – Southern University Athletics proudly announces the launch of Uncaged: Building Beyond the Bluff, a seven-month leadership development initiative designed to empower Jaguar student-athletes to excel beyond their respective sports.
  Funded through the NCAA Accelerating Academic Success Program (AASP) Grant, Uncaged is led by Tambria Bradford, Director of Student-Athlete Development and Academics, and Venessa Jacobs, Student-Athlete Support Coordinator. The program focuses on holistic development through leadership, mentorship, entrepreneurship, and personal branding, equipping Southern student-athletes to thrive beyond the bluff.
  Throughout the program, participants will engage in workshops, mentorship pairings, and collaborative experiences that strengthen their leadership and life skills. Each student-athlete will be partnered with a professional mentor who will guide them throughout the duration of the program, providing one-on-one support and career insight.
  The curriculum also features campus-wide partnerships with the Southern University Law Center, College of Business, Department of Mass Communication, Athletes for Hope, EFCU Financial, and more. These collaborations will cover topics such as contracts, NIL education, financial literacy, media training, and community impact. The program culminates in a capstone pitch, where each cohort member will present a philanthropic or business venture of their own creation.
  Undergraduate student Mykah Mares, Assistant Strategic Communications, is leading the marketing and personal branding component of Uncaged. With the program's motto "In Your Bag," Mares helped bring to life a visual campaign that showcases student-athletes as young business professionals who are balancing competition, academics, and entrepreneurship.
  The cohort's reveal shoot was staged in front of a vault, symbolizing both financial literacy and the concept of "being in your bag." The creative direction highlights the modern student-athlete as multidimensional, disciplined, driven, and investing in their future.
  "Uncaged: Building Beyond the Bluff represents the essence of Jaguar excellence by preparing our student-athletes not just for the next game, but for the next chapter of life," said Southern University Athletic Director Roman Banks. "We're proud to provide our athletes with the resources, mentorship, and exposure to become future leaders in business, community, and beyond."
  "This program is about going beyond what's expected. Our goal is to help student-athletes realize that their talents and influence extend far beyond their sport," said Tambria Bradford, Director of Student-Athlete Development and Academics. "Through Uncaged, they are building confidence, discovering their purpose, and creating impact that lasts long after their time on the bluff."

The 2025 Uncaged: Building Beyond the Bluff Cohort includes: Markeis Batiste – Football Xavier Bradley – Baseball Herman Brister III – Football Eva Clayton – Cheer San'aa Doss – Women's Soccer Jordan Felix – Volleyball Christopher Hall – Football Logan Hart – Volleyball Michael Jacobs – Basketball Kenneth Jackson – Baseball Kira Johnson – Softball Keeton Johnson – Track & Cross Country Omari Johnson – Baseball Wyatt King– Golf Keira Miracle-Tilford – Softball Mariah Mott – Volleyball Christian Phillips – Track & Field & Cross Country Jayden Rogers – Football Angel Stein  – Bowling Collins Spencer – Baseball Iyanah Taylor – Volleyball Rondisia Williams– Track & Field Kai Wince – Tennis

Through Uncaged: Building Beyond the Bluff, Southern University continues to invest in the holistic success of its student-athletes, celebrating those who are not only "in their bag" on the field but also in the classroom, the boardroom, and the community.

Baton Rouge, LA – Southern University and Associated Grocers met Friday to celebrate the one-year anniversary of the partnership between Associated Grocers, Inc. (AG) and the Southern University Men's Basketball Team. 

The Southern Men's Basketball team was able to hear from Roeshawn Peters, Corporate Marketing Manager and President of AGives!, Associated Grocers 501 c 3 non-profit affiliate, as well as Wilbur Fabre Jr., Sr. Director of Distribution and Vice President of AGives! Also in attendance was Deputy AD Rodney Kirschner, Care South CEO/Harwood Club Director Matt Valliere and Anna Jones and Judge Greggs of the 6th Man Club. 

Over the past year, the partnership has fueled the Southern Men's Basketball program. Associated Grocers has been an indispensable resource for the program, helping to supply the Jaguars with nutrition for our student-athletes.

Head Coach Kevin Johnson spoke about the value of the partnership, "Partnering with Associated Grocers, Inc. has elevated our program in ways that go beyond basketball. Their unwavering support has allowed us to build a stronger team, foster a deeper connection with the community, and provide our student-athletes with proper nutrition and establish healthy eating habits. We are excited to celebrate this milestone and look forward to growing this partnership in the years to come."

For more information about Associated Grocers, Inc. and their commitment to community development, visit agives.org and agbr.comto to locate AG retailers.

BATON ROUGE, La – The Southern University men's basketball program will embark on a six-day, five-night Foreign Tour and team bonding trip to the Bahamas.

The Jaguars are scheduled to depart on Saturday, August 10, for Nassau and return on Thursday, August 15.

"I want to thank [Director of Athletics] Roman Banks for helping fundraise and our donors for providing us with this great opportunity," said SU Head Coach Kevin Johnson. "This trip is extremely important to our program especially with so many new players. We get a chance to have practices before the trip and will spend a lot of time together not only on the court getting better, but off the court growing as team and get a chance to make unforgettable memories."

While abroad, the Jaguars will play the Bahamas All Stars, Raw Talent Elite and Lucayans Basketball at the Kendal GL Isaacs Gym as well as participate in team-building activities around the island.

Southern will also use this platform as a basketball team to give young athletes hope in their future aspirations by showing good attitudes and sportsmanship on and off the court.

NCAA rules allow college basketball programs to take a foreign tour every four years where teams can play exhibition games abroad against international competition.

In previous foreign tours, Southern visited the Bahamas in 2017 and Canada in 2013.
